title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 16
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Doctors and population in five regions, against a national figure of one doctor for every 400 people:

Amberley: 120 doctors, population 54,000
Brackwood: 85 doctors, population 30,600
Cheltmoor: 210 doctors, population 82,000
Dorsington: 45 doctors, population 22,500
Everton: 160 doctors, population 70,400

Which region comes closest to the national figure?
questions.explanation: People per doctor: Amberley 450, Brackwood 360, Cheltmoor 390, Dorsington 500, Everton 440. Cheltmoor is 9.52 away from 400, nearer than any other region. Brackwood is the best served at 360 people a doctor, but being furthest below the national figure is not the same as being closest to it.

questions.prompt:
Annual figures:

2016: 240
2017: 268
2018: 255
2019: 291
2020: 202
2021: 246
2022: 279
2023: 271
2024: 305

In how many years did the figure fall on the year before?
questions.explanation: Comparing each year with the one before it, the falls come in 2018, 2020, 2023 — 3 of the eight changes. The other five are rises. The steepest fall, in 2020, is much larger than the other two, but the question asks how many, not how far.

questions.prompt:
A ride, broken into four stretches:

The first 40 minutes: 12 km in 40 minutes
The next 30 minutes: 15 km in 30 minutes
The following 20 minutes: 6 km in 20 minutes
The last 60 minutes: 27 km in 60 minutes

Over which stretch was the cyclist fastest?
options: E. The speed was the same throughout
questions.explanation: Speeds are distance divided by time in hours: The first 40 minutes 18 km/h, The next 30 minutes 30 km/h, The following 20 minutes 18 km/h, The last 60 minutes 27 km/h. The cyclist was fastest over the stretch labelled "The next 30 minutes" at 30 km/h. The stretch covering the most ground, "The last 60 minutes", is 27 km, more than any other, but takes a full hour to do it.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 5, 8, 8, 11, 14, 17, 21

Every reading is then multiplied by 3. Which statement about the effect is accurate?
options: A. Only the mean is multiplied by 3
D. The mean, the median, the mode and the range are all multiplied by 3
E. The mean is multiplied by 3 but the median is not
questions.explanation: Before: mean 12, median 11, mode 8, range 16. After: mean 36, median 33, mode 24, range 48. Stretching the data multiplies the gaps between values as well as the values themselves, so the range moves too — unlike adding a constant, which shifts every value but leaves the range where it was.

questions.prompt:
A budget of GBP 52,500.00 is split between two departments in the ratio 4 : 3.

Select the amount each department receives.
options: E. The split cannot be worked out from a ratio alone
questions.explanation: The ratio has 7 parts, so one part is GBP 52,500.00 / 7 = GBP 7,500.00. Four parts is GBP 30,000.00 and three parts is GBP 22,500.00, and the two add back to GBP 52,500.00. Treating the ratio as tenths gives GBP 21,000.00 and GBP 15,750.00, which together fall GBP 15,750.00 short of the budget.

questions.prompt:
Units cost GBP 8.40 each, but an order of 500 or more takes 12% off the whole order.

Select the cost of ordering 480 units AND the cost of ordering 500.
questions.explanation: 480 units miss the threshold, so they cost 480 × GBP 8.40 = GBP 4,032.00. 500 units qualify: GBP 4,200.00 less 12% is GBP 3,696.00. Ordering 20 more units therefore costs GBP 336.00 less — the discount is worth more than the extra units cost.

questions.prompt:
Two products:

Product X: 1,200 sold at GBP 15.00, margin 40%
Product Y: 9,000 sold at GBP 4.00, margin 25%

Select the product with the higher margin AND the product that makes more profit in total.
options: A. Product X on both measures
B. Product Y on both measures
C. Product Y on margin; Product X on total profit
D. The two products are equal on both measures
E. Product X on margin; Product Y on total profit
questions.explanation: Margins are given: Product X 40%, Product Y 25%. Total profit is units multiplied by price multiplied by margin: Product X GBP 7,200.00 and Product Y GBP 9,000.00. The thinner margin is earned on seven and a half times as many units, so the better margin does not make the better business.

questions.prompt:
640 people are surveyed. 3/8 of them choose option A, and 2/5 of those who chose A are under 30.

Select the number choosing option A AND the number of those who are under 30.
options: A. 240 chose A; 256 of them under 30
B. 240 chose A; 96 of them under 30
C. 120 chose A; 96 of them under 30
D. 240 chose A; 120 of them under 30
E. 240 chose A; 240 of them under 30
questions.explanation: 3/8 of 640 is 240 people choosing option A. 2/5 of those 240 — not of the whole 640 — is 96. Taking 2/5 of everybody gives 256 and forgets that the second fraction applies only to the first group.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): annual visitors — Museum A 340,000, Museum B 96,000, Museum C 512,000

SOURCE 2 (table): public floor area — Museum A 8,500 square metres, Museum B 1,600 square metres, Museum C 11,600 square metres

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Crowding funds go to the museum carrying the most visitors for each square metre of public space."

Which museum receives the funds?
options: C. The three museums are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Visitors divided by floor area: Museum A 40 a square metre, Museum B 60 a square metre, Museum C 44 a square metre. Museum B is most crowded and is by far the smallest building. Museum C sees 512,000 visitors, more than five times as many, but has 11,600 square metres to spread them through.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Electric van sales rose 340% last year."

SOURCE 2 (table): diesel van sales fell 4%.

SOURCE 3 (table): before the year, electric vans were 1.2% of the market and diesel vans 78%.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Diesel still outsells electric by a wide margin, and the 340% rise is large because the starting base was tiny
B. Electric vans now outsell diesel vans
C. The market has switched to electric vans
D. Diesel sales fell by more vans than electric sales gained
E. Electric vans are now 340% of the market
questions.explanation: A 340% rise takes electric vans from 1.2% of the market to about 5.3%, while diesel falls from 78% to about 74.9% — still fourteen times as large. In share terms electric gained roughly 4.1 points while diesel lost about 3.1, so diesel did not fall by more than electric gained either. A percentage rise says nothing on its own about the size it started from.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): price — System A GBP 92,000.00, System B GBP 68,000.00, System C GBP 74,500.00

SOURCE 2 (table): capability score out of 100 — System A 91, System B 84, System C 88

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Choose the highest-scoring system that costs no more than GBP 75,000.00."

Which system is chosen?
options: D. All three score the same
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: System A scores highest at 91 but costs GBP 92,000.00, over the GBP 75,000.00 ceiling, so it is out before its score matters. Of the two within budget, System B scores 84 at GBP 68,000.00 and System C scores 88 at GBP 74,500.00, so System C wins on 88 against 84.

questions.prompt:
A report concludes that new packaging cut breakages.

SOURCE 1 (table): breakages fell from 4.8% of shipments to 1.9% after the packaging changed.

SOURCE 2 (note): the same carrier handled every shipment before and after the change.

SOURCE 3 (table): shipment volumes were similar in the two periods.

Which source most needs to be true if the packaging is to be credited with the fall?
options: C. None of them: the conclusion holds on its own
E. Source 2, that the carrier did not change
questions.explanation: Source 1 records the fall that needs explaining, and source 3 rules out a change of scale, which matters less because the figures are already percentages. Source 2 is what rules out the most obvious rival explanation: had a different carrier taken over at the same time, the handling rather than the packaging could account for the whole improvement.

questions.prompt:
What is the perimeter of a rectangle?

(1) Its area is 48 square centimetres.
(2) It measures 8 cm by 6 cm.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) fits 8 by 6, 12 by 4 and 16 by 3, with perimeters of 28, 32 and 38 cm, so it settles nothing. (2) gives both sides, so the perimeter is 2 × (8 + 6) = 28 cm. The two are consistent, since 8 by 6 does have an area of 48.

questions.prompt:
Is the positive integer n divisible by 4?

(1) n is divisible by 8.
(2) n is a multiple of 12.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4, so (1) gives a definite yes. Every multiple of 12 is also a multiple of 4, since 12 is 4 times 3, so (2) gives the same yes. Each statement alone settles the question, and 24 satisfies both at once.

questions.prompt:
What is the total of a restaurant bill?

(1) The food and drink came to GBP 84.
(2) A service charge of 12.5% was added.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives the amount before service but not the service, and (2) gives a percentage with nothing to apply it to. Together, GBP 84 plus 12.5% is GBP 94.50. Each statement supplies exactly one of the two things the total needs.

questions.prompt:
How many pupils are in a class?

(1) There are 3 boys for every 2 girls, and there are 12 girls.
(2) There are more boys than girls.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), 12 girls means six groups of two, so there are six groups of three boys — 18 boys and 30 pupils in all. (2) is true of that class but of countless others too, so it fixes nothing on its own.

questions.prompt:
Which site generates the most electricity in a year?

Site | Capacity (MW) | Capacity factor | Staff | Age (years)
Ardennes | 240 | 34% | 45 | 12
Blaxton | 90 | 52% | 22 | 4
Cranmere | 410 | 28% | 78 | 19
Dellow | 160 | 41% | 31 | 8
Eastrigg | 320 | 47% | 58 | 6
Fothergill | 70 | 58% | 15 | 2
questions.explanation: Annual output is capacity multiplied by the hours in a year multiplied by the capacity factor: Ardennes 715 GWh, Blaxton 410 GWh, Cranmere 1,006 GWh, Dellow 575 GWh, Eastrigg 1,318 GWh, Fothergill 356 GWh. Eastrigg generates the most while leading on neither column: Cranmere has 410 MW of capacity and Fothergill runs at 58%. A large plant that runs less than a third of the time is beaten by a slightly smaller one that runs nearly half.

questions.prompt:
Which site generates the most electricity for each member of staff?

Site | Capacity (MW) | Capacity factor | Staff | Age (years)
Ardennes | 240 | 34% | 45 | 12
Blaxton | 90 | 52% | 22 | 4
Cranmere | 410 | 28% | 78 | 19
Dellow | 160 | 41% | 31 | 8
Eastrigg | 320 | 47% | 58 | 6
Fothergill | 70 | 58% | 15 | 2
questions.explanation: Output divided by staff: Ardennes 15.88 GWh a head, Blaxton 18.63 GWh a head, Cranmere 12.89 GWh a head, Dellow 18.54 GWh a head, Eastrigg 22.72 GWh a head, Fothergill 23.71 GWh a head. Fothergill leads at 23.71 and is the smallest site in the table. Eastrigg generates the most electricity overall but employs 58 people to do it.

questions.prompt:
How many sites run above the median capacity factor and are less than 10 years old?

Site | Capacity (MW) | Capacity factor | Staff | Age (years)
Ardennes | 240 | 34% | 45 | 12
Blaxton | 90 | 52% | 22 | 4
Cranmere | 410 | 28% | 78 | 19
Dellow | 160 | 41% | 31 | 8
Eastrigg | 320 | 47% | 58 | 6
Fothergill | 70 | 58% | 15 | 2
questions.explanation: The median capacity factor is 44%. Above it: Blaxton 52%, Eastrigg 47%, Fothergill 58%. Under 10 years old: Blaxton 4, Dellow 8, Eastrigg 6, Fothergill 2. On both counts: Blaxton, Eastrigg, Fothergill — 3. The newest sites do tend to run hardest, though one young site does not.

questions.prompt:
How many sites run above the median capacity factor while holding below the median capacity?

Site | Capacity (MW) | Capacity factor | Staff | Age (years)
Ardennes | 240 | 34% | 45 | 12
Blaxton | 90 | 52% | 22 | 4
Cranmere | 410 | 28% | 78 | 19
Dellow | 160 | 41% | 31 | 8
Eastrigg | 320 | 47% | 58 | 6
Fothergill | 70 | 58% | 15 | 2
questions.explanation: The medians are 44% capacity factor and 200 MW of capacity. Above on factor: Blaxton, Eastrigg, Fothergill. Below on capacity: Blaxton, Dellow, Fothergill. On both: Blaxton and Fothergill — 2. The small sites run hardest here, but not all of them, and the hardest-running large site is missing from the list.
